_new_tests_audited: tests/report-screen-shape.test.tsx was read assertion by assertion, and two of its five claims do NOT hold. (1) R18's no-sub-label rule does not catch the sub-label that broke R18 for a whole round. Its check is queryByText(/\. /) — text containing a period FOLLOWED BY A SPACE — and the offending string was description="Finish this ticket in your browser, where you can attach them" (d9f63efa), which has no period at all. Proven, not argued: the SettingRow DOM was rebuilt in jsdom with the project's own @testing-library and the test's exact two-hop selector, and the real regression came back GREEN, as did any other one-sentence sub-label; only a two-sentence one goes red. What that test DOES pin, and pins well, is three checkbox rows and three (i) buttons under the heading. (2) R2's marker fix is pinned as /list-decimal/ and /ml-\d/ on the <ol> — but the previous broken state was `list-decimal list-inside ml-…`, which satisfies both regexes, so re-adding list-inside would leave it green; and marker clipping is a layout fact jsdom cannot see at any rate. The other three are real: R6/R21's footer test counts buttons INSIDE the footer div, and the shipped-then-rejected footer had three there, so it goes red; R17's queryByRole(/assistant/i)-is-null-before-you-open-it catches exactly the defect that failed the row; R22 fails red if the version line is deleted or hardcoded (the old 'YouCoded 1.2.4 · Linux x64 · Electron 41.10.3' fails both of its assertions). The file's header claim that it pins 'the full-width button (R6)' is wrong about which screen: R6 is the CONTRIBUTE setup button, and that test measures the ticket screen's footer.
